name: Mount Oberon
bio_draft: The Prom's signature summit walk, a granite climb with 360-degree views over the peninsula and Bass Strait.

facts.claim: Walk starts at Telegraph Saddle Carpark and winds through tall eucalypts to the summit
Summit has panoramic views of the coastline, Tidal River and offshore islands
Grade 4, 6.8 km and 2 hours return; the last 100 m is a steep climb of timber and granite steps

name: Wilsons Promontory Lightstation
bio_draft: Historic granite lighthouse and keepers' cottages at South East Point, reached by a long coastal walk.

facts.claim: Granite lighthouse at South East Point, lit in 1859, southernmost lighthouse on mainland Australia
Stands 100 m above Bass Strait; reached only on foot, 20 km from Telegraph Saddle Carpark or via the Southern Circuit
Overnight stays in the historic residences need advance booking; no supplies on site

access_note: Hike-in only (about 20 km each way); overnight stay in the lightstation is booked ahead and is an extra, not the price.

name: Mount Bishop
bio_draft: A summit walk of around 2.5 hours with views over Squeaky Beach and Whisky Bay.

facts.claim: Walk starts at Lilly Pilly Gully Carpark and climbs through warm temperate rainforest and dry eucalypt bush
Summit views over the west coast of Wilsons Promontory and its offshore islands
Grade 3, 7.4 km and 2.5 hours return

name: Tongue Point
bio_draft: A coastal headland walk from Darby River with sweeping views along the Prom's western shore.

facts.claim: Darby River to Tongue Point Walk climbs an ancient sand dune then follows a weathered granite headland
Granite tors and a semi-detached boulder-covered island mark the end; a short detour reaches Fairy Cove
Grade 4, 3.8 km and 2 hours one way from Darby River Carpark

name: Lilly Pilly Gully
bio_draft: A short rainforest nature walk of fern gullies and tall eucalypts, easy enough for prams.

facts.claim: Lilly Pilly Gully Nature Walk passes through shaded warm temperate rainforest
Wallabies, Eastern Yellow Robins and Superb Fairy-wrens are common
Grade 2, 5.2 km return, 1.5 hours; flat gravel track suited to families and limited mobility

name: Mallacoota
bio_draft: Remote inlet town on the Victorian coast, the gateway to Croajingolong with beaches, lakes and bushwalks.

facts.claim: Town in East Gippsland, the last township on Victoria's east coast before the NSW border
Popular for boating, fishing, walking, swimming, birdwatching and surfing
Known for the inlet estuary of Top Lake and Bottom Lake, surrounded by Croajingolong National Park

name: Point Hicks Lightstation
bio_draft: Granite lighthouse where Cook's crew first sighted Australia's east coast, with tours and keepers' cottages.

facts.claim: The prominent granite headland of Point Hicks was Captain James Cook's first sighting of mainland Australia.
The historic lighthouse sits in Croajingolong National Park, where visitors can join a lighthouse tour or stay in the keeper's cottages.
Whales can be seen on their annual migration from October to May.

access_note: Page flags 'area is closed' banner and Change of Conditions; earlier Parks Victoria notice said lighthouse, Thurra River campground and tracks closed after 2019/20 fires. Current open status not confirmed.

name: Gabo Island Lightstation
bio_draft: Pink-granite lighthouse on an island reached by boat or plane, beside a large little penguin colony.

facts.claim: Gabo Island Lighthouse, built 1858 to 1862 from pink granite found on the island, is 47 metres high, the second tallest lighthouse in Australia.
It is the only operating island lighthouse in Victoria, just off Croajingolong National Park east of Mallacoota.
Access to the island is by private boat or aircraft; day visitors are welcome and must book lighthouse tours with a licensed tour operator.

access_note: Island access sometimes restricted by weather; tours via licensed operator (price not found).
unresolved: Penguin colony claim in draft bio not verified from fetched sources

name: Wilderness Coast Walk
bio_draft: A multi-day coastal walk from Sydenham Inlet to Mallacoota through the park's remote beaches and inlets.

facts.claim: A multi-day hike taking in isolated stretches of coastline, pristine river estuaries and untouched landscapes, far from civilisation.
The track is open all the way from Bemm River to Mallacoota; hikers must self-navigate with map and compass.

access_note: Draft bio says Sydenham Inlet to Mallacoota; Parks Victoria says Bemm River to Mallacoota. Flood and fire damage make some sections harder to navigate. Camping at campgrounds may need booking/fees; not the walk's price.

name: Thurra River Sand Dunes
bio_draft: Giant sand dunes at the mouth of the Thurra River, near Point Hicks, reached on foot from the campground.

facts.claim: The dunes tower 30 metres over the coast below and are the biggest sand dunes in Victoria.
They are a short walk from Thurra River Campground, near Point Hicks.

access_note: Thurra River campground and nearby tracks were closed after 2019/20 fires per an earlier Parks Victoria notice; current status unconfirmed.

name: Fly Cove Walk
bio_draft: A boardwalk and track from Wingan Inlet to Fly Cove across paperbark wetlands, in the park's remote west.

facts.claim: The walk starts at Wingan Inlet Campground and leads to pristine sandy beaches of Croajingolong National Park.
Fur seals can be seen basking on rocky islets at Fly Cove.

access_note: Wingan Inlet Rapids Walk is listed closed; Fly Cove Walk not listed as closed.

name: Lakes Entrance
bio_draft: Tourist town where the lakes meet Bass Strait, with a footbridge to the ocean beach, cruises and seafood.

facts.claim: Town in the Shire of East Gippsland, about 320 km east of Melbourne.
It sits beside a managed, artificial channel connecting the Gippsland Lakes to Bass Strait.
Local tourism listings cover cruises, fishing charters, dolphin cruises and beaches.

name: Metung
bio_draft: Harbour village on Bancroft Bay with boating, a hot springs spa and a back beach.

facts.claim: Town on a small peninsula between Lake King and Bancroft Bay on the Gippsland Lakes, 31 km south-east of Bairnsdale
Between Bairnsdale and Lakes Entrance, 314 km east of Melbourne
Legend Rock, tied to a Gunai/Kurnai story, stands beside the boardwalk in Metung Marina on Bancroft Bay
Metung Hot Springs (separate paid venue, about $55 adult per third-party reports, not verified from its own site)

bio_draft: A kitsch roadside museum of seashells with a giant octopus on its roof, at Lakes Entrance.

facts.claim: Griffiths Sea Shell Museum and Marine Display (official name) is at 125 Esplanade, Lakes Entrance
Collection of marine and land shells, sea creatures, corals and sponges from around the world, a 10 m coral reef and an aquarium of Bass Strait sea life
Described as one of Australia's largest private collections of natural sea life, over 90,000 shells and creatures; established 1962

name: Bairnsdale
bio_draft: East Gippsland's service town and gateway to the lakes, and the regional hub for East Gippsland.

facts.claim: City in East Gippsland and the commercial hub of the region, seat of the Shire of East Gippsland
Urban population 17,666 at June 2023; one of eastern Victoria's major regional centres alongside Traralgon and Sale
31 km north-west of Metung on the way to the Gippsland Lakes

name: Cape Liptrap Coastal Park
bio_draft: Coastal park of tilted limestone cliffs, a lighthouse, historic lime kilns and quiet beaches.

facts.claim: Coastal park from the sand barrier of Point Smythe to the sheltered waters of Waratah Bay
Ruins of lime kilns in the cliffs at Walkerville South, from a lime port that operated 1875 to 1926
Cape Liptrap Lighthouse, established 1913, current structure from 1951, still operating
Coastal walks between Venus Bay and Waratah Bay, including Limeburners Walk; beach camping on Waratah Bay

name: Bunurong Marine National Park
bio_draft: Marine park of rock platforms and pools along the Bunurong coast, good for low-tide rock-pooling.

facts.claim: 2,046 ha marine national park on the Bass Strait coast between Inverloch and Wonthaggi
Extensive intertidal sandstone rock platforms with rockpools; best visited within an hour or so of low tide
Highest diversity of intertidal and shallow subtidal invertebrates in eastern Victoria
Port Jackson sharks rest under ledges at Eagles Nest and Twin Reefs

name: Agnes Falls
bio_draft: A 59 m waterfall, among the highest single-drop falls in Victoria, a short walk from the car park.

facts.claim: Agnes River drops 59 m over rocks into a gorge in the Strzelecki Ranges (Agnes Falls Scenic Reserve)
A 200 m walking track leads from the car park to the falls viewing area
Short drive from Toora or Welshpool; falls are at their best in wet seasons and after heavy rain
Picnic and birdwatching in a pocket of old forest and native bushland

name: Wonthaggi State Coal Mine
bio_draft: Former state coal mine with underground tours run by Parks Victoria's guides.

facts.claim: Former state-owned black coal mine in Wonthaggi, operational 1910 to 1968, now a heritage state park.
Entry to the aboveground attractions is free, starting at the Visitor's Centre with a short film and a heritage trail map.
Guided underground tours led by Parks Victoria staff and volunteers last 1-1.5 hours; children must be 5 or older.

access_note: Underground tours reported closed until further notice for major maintenance (visitbasscoast.com.au listing; Parks Victoria page shows a closed notice). Aboveground attractions free. Adult underground tour $25.50 (family $63.70).

name: Coal Creek Community Park and Museum
bio_draft: Recreated 19th-century coal-mining village of around 50 buildings at Korumburra.

facts.claim: Recreated coal-mining village with around 50 buildings dating from the 1870s to the 1920s, at 12 Silkstone Road, Korumburra.
Founded in 1974 to give the old Korumburra Courthouse a new home, and managed by South Gippsland Shire Council.
Entry is free with no bookings required.

name: Great Southern Rail Trail
bio_draft: A 129 km rail trail from Nyora to Alberton through dairy country, with towns and cafes along the way.

facts.claim: Rail trail of about 130 km through South Gippsland dairy farmland, linking 14 towns from Nyora to Alberton.
Surface is crushed granite and fine gravel, suitable for walking, cycling and horse riding.
The Fish Creek to Foster section climbs past Mount Hoddle with views of Wilsons Promontory and Corner Inlet.
Managed by South Gippsland Shire Council.

access_note: Length reported 129-136 km depending on source; Nyora to Alberton/Yarram.

facts.claim: Town in the foothills of the Strzelecki Ranges, 135 km south-east of Melbourne.
Population 5,869 at the 2021 census; the main service town of South Gippsland.

facts.claim: City in Gippsland and council seat of the Shire of Wellington, about 19,000 people with its surrounds.
Gippsland Art Gallery at 70 Foster Street is in the city.

name: Gippsland Art Gallery
bio_draft: A free regional gallery in Sale with a collection of around 5,000 works and changing exhibitions.

facts.claim: Regional public gallery in Sale at Port of Sale (Wellington Centre), 70 Foster Street, run by the Shire of Wellington.
Focus on the natural environment and artists based in Gippsland.
Permanent display of the textile art of Annemieke Mein, and a Borun & Tuk gallery of local First Nations art.
